If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Saving the same host with different categories succeeds without uniqueness enforcement, but imports select only the first record and silently ignore the other saved mapping.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue: EmbeddableHost model has no uniqueness validation on the 'host' field (line 2 only validates format), and the record_for_host method (lines 10-17) uses .first which would return only one record if duplicates exist. This means users could save the same host with different categories, but only the first record would be used when looking up the category for embedding. The diff shows no uniqueness constraint in the model or migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 — Changing the enabled category chooser while a save is pending makes the success callback display the new selection although the server saved the earlier category.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the save action in embeddable-host.js.es6 lines 29-38, the code captures `this.get('categoryId')` in `props.category_id` before the async save, then in the success callback uses `this.get('categoryId')` again to set the category. If the user changes the category chooser while the save is pending, the success callback will use the new categoryId value rather than the one that was actually saved to the server. This is a race condition bug where the UI could display incorrect data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Migrating configured URLs verbatim while lookup compares only URI host makes previously accepted scheme/path entries stop embedding after upgrade.
matched_golden_ids: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same core problem as the golden comment: the migration inserts embeddable_hosts data verbatim (raw SQL) without normalization, while the new lookup mechanism compares only the URI host. This means existing entries with schemes (http://, https://) or path segments won't match properly after migration, breaking existing embedding configurations. Both comments point to the same data migration normalization issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/site_settings.yml:762 — Removing embeddable_hosts and embed_category without a compatibility layer breaks plugins and automation using the established SiteSetting and admin-settings contracts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows removal of 'embeddable_hosts' and 'embed_category' from config/site_settings.yml (lines 762-763 area), and the migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb migrates existing data to the new EmbeddableHost model and then deletes these settings. While the migration handles existing data, this is a breaking change for any external plugins or automation that relied on SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts or SiteSetting.embed_category. The finding correctly identifies a real architectural concern - there's no deprecation period or compatibility layer. However, this is a design decision rather than a bug, as the migration does properly transfer existing data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — The API accepts and persists host:port values but lookup discards the request port, so successfully configured port-specific hosts are always rejected.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff, in `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the validation regex on line 2 allows port numbers (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and the `before_validation` block only strips the protocol and path, preserving the port in the stored host value. However, in `record_for_host` method (lines 10-17), it extracts `uri.host` which in Ruby's URI library returns only the hostname without the port. So if someone configures 'example.com:8080' as an embeddable host, the lookup will compare 'example.com' (from uri.host) against 'example.com:8080' (stored value), which won't match. This is a real bug where port-specific hosts would be stored but never matched.

matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same problem as the golden comment - that accessing [0] on the query result without checking if rows exist will cause the migration to fail/abort when no embed_category setting exists. Both comments point to the same bug: dereferencing [0] on an empty result set causes a crash/abort.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Migrated hosts retain previously supported URL schemes and paths because raw INSERT bypasses normalization, so existing embeds fail the new hostname lookup.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue in the migration. Looking at the migration code, it reads existing hosts from site_settings and inserts them directly: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. The old setting `embeddable_hosts` could contain values like 'http://eviltrout.com' or 'https://example.com/1234' (as shown in the test at line 70-72 of embed_controller_spec.rb). The migration does a raw INSERT that bypasses the model's before_validation hook which strips 'http://', 'https://' and paths. Meanwhile, the new EmbeddableHost.record_for_host method (lines 10-17 of embeddable_host.rb) extracts just the hostname from the URI and does a case-insensitive lookup. If migrated data contains 'http://eviltrout.com', the lookup for 'eviltrout.com' won't match. This is a real data migration bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Saving a permitted hostname with a port retains that port but lookup compares only URI.host, so the saved host can never authorize its own embedding URL.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real bug. In embeddable_host.rb, the before_validation hook strips the protocol and path from the host (lines 5-7), but if a port is included (e.g., 'example.com:8080'), it's retained in the saved host. However, in record_for_host (lines 10-17), the lookup uses `uri.host` which returns only the hostname without the port. So if you save 'example.com:8080', the database stores 'example.com:8080', but when checking if a host is allowed, it compares against 'example.com' (from URI.host), which won't match. This is a correctness bug where hosts with ports can never authorize their own embedding URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Limiting top-level domains to five letters rejects valid hosts such as example.technology that the previous host allowlist supported.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2 a regex validation: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 characters. This would reject valid TLDs like .technology, .photography, .international, etc. which have more than 5 characters. The previous implementation in site_setting.rb used a simple string comparison without TLD length restrictions, so this is a regression that breaks previously working functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — Indexing the category query before checking for no match makes the migration crash on the default blank embed_category, blocking upgrades.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration code in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, lines 10-14 show: `category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. When embed_category is blank or doesn't match any category, the query returns no rows, so `[0]` returns nil, and calling `['id']` on nil will raise a NoMethodError. The code does check `if category_id == 0` afterward to fall back to uncategorized, but the crash happens before that check when trying to access the result. This is a real bug that would cause the migration to fail on systems with blank/invalid embed_category settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Copying legacy host values without stripping schemes and paths causes previously accepted URL-form hosts to stop authorizing embeds after migration.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 copies legacy host values directly from the old site_settings table without any transformation. However, the new EmbeddableHost model (lines 5-7 in embeddable_host.rb) has a before_validation callback that strips 'http://' and 'https://' prefixes and paths. The old embeddable_hosts setting allowed URL-form entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' (as shown in the removed tests in site_setting_spec.rb). When these are migrated directly via INSERT, they bypass the model's before_validation callback, so hosts like 'http://eviltrout.com' remain in the database with the scheme prefix. The host_allowed? method uses record_for_host which extracts just the hostname from the URL being checked and compares it with a lowercase match. If the stored host is 'http://eviltrout.com' but the query is for 'eviltrout.com', the match will fail, breaking embed authorization for previously working hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — Deleting both legacy settings inside an irreversible change migration leaves rollback unable to restore embedding configuration and can disable all existing embeds.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb uses `def change` which Rails attempts to make reversible, but the `execute` statements for DELETE and INSERT are not automatically reversible. The migration deletes the old site_settings ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category') after migrating data to the new table. If rolled back, Rails cannot restore those deleted settings, potentially leaving embedding configuration in a broken state. This is a legitimate architectural concern about data migration safety, though it's a one-way migration by design. The finding correctly identifies that rollback would not restore the original configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5 — The unreferenced saveChanges action and its no-op PUT endpoint add dead client/server API surface that future maintainers must preserve without providing any behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at the diff: 1) admin-embedding.js.es6 defines a saveChanges action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` with an empty object. 2) The embedding_controller.rb's update method just renders the same serialized data without actually updating anything - it's a no-op. 3) The embedding.hbs template doesn't have any button or UI element that triggers saveChanges. This creates dead code that adds maintenance burden. While not a bug (it doesn't break anything), it's a legitimate architectural concern about incomplete/unused code being added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Every public embed request now performs an uncached database lookup with no usable host index, so embed traffic adds a database round trip and full host-table scan per request.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that EmbeddableHost.record_for_host (line 10-17 in app/models/embeddable_host.rb) performs a database query with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` on every embed request. Looking at the diff, there's no index added in the migration (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb only creates the table with host and category_id columns, no index). The query uses `lower(host)` which would prevent using a standard index anyway. This is a legitimate performance concern for a feature that handles public traffic, though it's not a bug per se - the code works correctly, it's just potentially inefficient at scale.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The migration dereferences an absent embed_category row, so sites that never persisted this optional setting abort the deployment.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at lines 10-12 executes a query to find the category_id from embed_category site setting. If no row exists (the setting was never configured), the query returns an empty result, and accessing [0]['id'] on nil/empty result would cause an error. The code then falls back to uncategorized_category_id only if category_id == 0, but if the first query returns no rows, accessing [0] on an empty result set would fail before reaching that check. This is a real bug that would cause migration failures on sites that never set embed_category.

matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment - that calling sub! on self.host when host is nil will cause an error. The golden comment says it raises NoMethodError, while the candidate describes it as causing HTTP 500 responses, but both are describing the same underlying bug: the before_validation callback doesn't handle the case where host is nil before calling sub! on it.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: the update and destroy methods don't validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record, and when the lookup returns nil (for missing/stale IDs), calling methods on nil will cause errors (NoMethodError/HTTP 500). Both point to the same bug in the same controller methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — The delete promise has no rejection handler, so a failed DELETE gives administrators no error feedback and leaves the operation ambiguous.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 46 in embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but there is no `.catch()` handler for the promise. In contrast, the save action at line 38 properly handles errors with `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. This is a real inconsistency where a failed DELETE request would silently fail without user feedback, which is a verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Interpolating legacy host URLs directly into SQL allows apostrophes in stored URL paths to abort the migration and crafted values to alter the statement.

adjudication.rationale: The migration at line 25 uses string interpolation to insert host values directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. The host values come from a site setting that could contain apostrophes or malicious SQL. This is a SQL injection vulnerability - if a host value contains a single quote, it would break the SQL statement or allow injection attacks. The code should use parameterized queries or proper escaping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5 — The inheritance-only assertion leaves create, update, destroy, validation failure, and default-category behavior untested, so regressions in the new administrative CRUD API can ship undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new spec file at spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb only tests that the controller inherits from AdminController, but doesn't test the actual CRUD operations (create, update, destroy) implemented in app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb. The diff shows the controller has create, update, destroy actions with specific logic (save_host method, category_id handling, error responses), but none of this is tested. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:30 — No component test exercises save, failed save, confirmed deletion, or either cancel branch, so the primary host-editing workflow has no behavioral regression protection.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new embeddable-host.js.es6 component with significant logic including save(), delete(), and cancel() actions that handle state management, API calls, error handling, and conditional behavior (isNew vs existing records). The finding correctly identifies that no component tests are added for this new functionality. While spec files are added for the controllers (embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb, embedding_controller_spec.rb), they only verify inheritance. The JavaScript component's behavioral logic (save with error handling, confirmed deletion, cancel with rollback) has no test coverage in this diff. This is a legitimate concern for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196 — The new plural `_ids` hydration branch has no test for found, missing, or empty associations, so a framework-wide serialization regression could remain hidden.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new `_ids` (plural) hydration branch added in store.js.es6 (lines 196-202) lacks comprehensive test coverage for edge cases. Looking at the test file changes, the tests only verify the happy path where colors are found (fruitCols.length, fruitCols[0].get('id')). The new code has a fallback `|| []` for when hydration fails, but there's no test verifying behavior when IDs reference missing objects or when the array is empty. This is a legitimate concern about test coverage for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to a real concern in the migration at db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb. Looking at the migration code, it attempts to migrate data from site_settings to the new embeddable_hosts table. The migration has potential issues: (1) If 'embed_category' setting doesn't exist or returns no rows, category_id becomes 0, then falls back to uncategorized_category_id, but if that also doesn't exist, category_id could be 0/nil which would violate the 'null: false' constraint on category_id. However, this is a migration concern rather than a bug - the migration does have fallback logic and handles the case where embeddable_hosts setting is empty.
